Strengthening of family ties through ORV use
#98 9. State of Colorado  felt that paragraph in draft environmental statement on ORV experiences is purely conjecture, and that statement should describe feelings of sheer terror regarding ORV as well as the exhilirating feeling of ORV user.
#106 10. Interior  National Park Service  Washington Office  felt that statement should contain evidence to support statement regarding strengthening of family ties through ORV use.
In contrast to these negative responses, the Department has received innumerable letters since the issuance of Executive Order 11644 in which the various kinds of ORV riders point out that they participate in ORV riding as a family sport and that it keeps the family together in regard to other related recreational activities such as camping. Also, our contacts in the field with user groups support the "family phenomenon" of ORV rallies, events, and vacations. Further, many ORV-user-oriented magazines and communications from ORV user organizations contain similar information about these ORV activities being a family sport and riding together and participating in related recreational activities served to keep the family together in their leisure time.
The final environmental statement has been modified to reflect the differing viewpoints on this issue. We recognize that others may argue that comparable statements regarding camping, fishing, and other such activities could be made, and, therefore, the point is not unique.
15. Discussion regarding the necessity for additional research concerning ORV effects. All elements of ORV concern seem to agree that much more needs to be known about the ORV user and the ORV environmental relationships, and that research is necessary to obtain such information.
16. Organized Off-Road Vehicle Events. Several comments were received concerning the advisability of holding organized events on Interior lands. The Department's ORV regulations specify that no person or association of persons may conduct any race, rally, meet, contest, or other type of organized event involving the use of off-road vehicles on public lands without first obtaining a permit from the authorized officer in charge of the lands to be used for such event.
